title: Single-task smoke test (cheapest scenario)
description: Deliberately the cheapest, simplest scenario in the library -- exists so `npm run battle -- --scenario single-task-smoke --model haiku` can prove the whole harness's plumbing end-to-end without spending much on the live smoke test (see docs/BATTLE-TESTING.md). RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-25 (netadvanced/vikunja-mcp#28 C1): optimalCallCount reasoning at the time -- create-project (1) + create-task with priority set at creation (1) = 2, with setup-kanban's 1-call route (PR #175) deliberately NOT credited because it required a fabricated placeholder column. RE-BASELINED 2026-09-02 (issue #202): that premise is stale -- `setup-kanban`'s `columns` argument became optional (issue #185), and its columns-less form (`title` + `tasks`, no `columns` at all) reaches 1 call with ZERO fabrication: no placeholder column, no Kanban view or bucket touched at all (same precedent as labels-due-date-combo.json and mixed-priority-batch.json). The scenario's designated role -- simplest, most deterministic scenario for a cheap live-smoke run (tests/battle/scenario.test.ts's 'single-task-smoke remains the designated cheap live-smoke-test scenario', which already anticipates and allows this and only requires `optimalCallCount <= 3`) -- is unaffected by an even cheaper honest floor; a haiku run already reaches 1 call unprompted (issue #202's evidence table). New optimum: setup-kanban with title + one task carrying priority 3, no columns (1).
promptTemplate: Create a project called "{{prefix}}Smoke Test" and add one task called "{{prefix}}hello world" with priority 3.
